original_test_intent: Prove BMC user creation, authentication, privilege/password editing and one-attempt lockout behavior across three approved temporary role profiles without affecting production or recovery accounts.
original_method: Snapshot account/policy baseline and break-glass access; create three uniquely named temporary accounts with Administrator, Operator and ReadOnly roles; verify fresh logins and owner-defined allowed/denied actions; apply the approved role-transition/password matrix and re-verify; set threshold 1, make exactly one wrong attempt against a dedicated disposable account and verify denial; then restore policy and remove/disable all test identities.
manual_activity: The security owner approves names, role transitions, secrets and boundary actions; an operator authorizes each account/policy mutation and maintains independent break-glass access while protected automation collects results.
required_inputs: Complete redacted account and policy baseline
Explicit edited-role transition for each account
Protected initial and replacement password generation/injection
Expected allowed/denied action matrix per role
safety_requirements: Never touch production, service or recovery accounts
Never expose passwords, hashes, tokens or cookies
Verify break-glass access before every lockout-policy change
Do not equate successful login with correct role enforcement
Use exactly one planned wrong attempt against the disposable account
Do not retry a failed login automatically
Stop on privilege escalation, unexpected lockout or fallback loss
Remove/disable all temporary accounts and restore policy
Do not clear audit or SEL logs
agent_execution_scope: Create and edit only explicitly approved temporary identities
Verify fresh logins and safe role-specific allowed/denied probes
Execute exactly one approved wrong-password attempt
Read back lockout and policy state
Remove/disable test accounts, restore baseline and report without verdict
engineer_actions: Approve account names, roles, transitions and boundary probes
Authorize threshold mutation and disposable lockout
Resolve access incidents and own PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Account lists are baseline evidence only; they do not create users, authenticate them, edit role/password, enforce boundaries or demonstrate threshold-1 lockout.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: With security approval, run the three temporary account create/login/role-boundary/edit/re-login transactions, then one dedicated threshold-1 wrong-password lockout, followed by complete account/policy cleanup and break-glass verification.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Three named role classes, edit/password, threshold 1, one wrong attempt and 20/20-minute estimates remain; exact edit targets are required inputs rather than guessed.

modernized_recommendation.status: SECURITY-APPROVED THREE-ROLE ACCOUNT AND LOCKOUT LIFECYCLE
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a transaction matrix per temporary account containing initial role, safe boundary probes, login, approved role/password edit, repeated probes, final cleanup, plus a separate one-attempt lockout record for the disposable identity.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds explicit role semantics, secret custody, recovery and cleanup while replacing the read-only inventory shortcut with the functional lifecycle.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Listing users proves existence only; login proves authentication only; authorization boundaries, edited state and lockout require distinct evidence.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A threshold of one magnifies operator or automation errors and role edits may terminate sessions or grant unintended authority, so no blind retries are safe.

project_override_considerations: The Project must select safe read-only/low-impact probes for each role and specify every edited-role destination. Row 1588 must repeat independent source identity and review even if execution is later deduplicated by an approved test plan.
expected_evidence: Redacted BMC/account/policy baseline, approvals and recovery proof
Protected creation/readback for three temporary roles with no secrets
Fresh-login and owner-defined allowed/denied boundary results before edits
Explicit role/password edit results and repeated login/boundary evidence
Threshold-1 write/readback, exactly one wrong attempt and lockout/unlock result
Policy restoration, all test-account cleanup, break-glass/audit/SEL evidence and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure and Criteria consistently require the same create/login/edit/lockout lifecycle. Missing destination roles and cleanup are readiness/safety inputs, not competing source targets.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The workflow is identifiable and becomes safe with normal security-owner inputs, supported account APIs, protected secrets, break-glass access and exact role/cleanup matrices.

review_improvement: Restores every omitted functional checkpoint and separates authentication, authorization, mutation and lockout evidence while protecting recovery identities from the threshold-1 hazard.
independent_technical_reasoning: BMC user-management correctness spans four different state machines: account provisioning, authentication, authorization and lockout. A user list observes only provisioning; each later transition needs its own fresh session and least-privilege probe, and the deliberately failed authentication must be isolated because a one-attempt threshold offers no margin for accidental retries.
